title: Autocheck: VPC convergence and model initialize routine
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement an automated post-deployment convergence and initialization routine for VPC/private deployments. This ticket covers a compact 'autocheck' run that executes immediately after Terraform completes apply and after conductor signals 'completed'. The routine performs API readiness validation (including auth and TLS), verifies model binary load and KV cache warming behavior, executes a fast smoke generation suite across pinned model families, and produces machine-readable results that can gate rollbacks or signal successful convergence to release pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Autocheck runs automatically after terraform apply (hooked to deploy CI step) and reports a single JSON summary to the deployment artifact store.
API readiness: 95th pct request latency < 250ms for control ping endpoint and health endpoint returns 200 + expected metadata (model_version, node_count, kvcache_status).

Model load tests: for each pinned model variant, at least one worker reports successful load within configured timeout (90s) and returns inference for a sample prompt within 2x expected latency baseline.
KV cache validation: prefix cache hit rate increases after running a warmup seedset and eviction behavior is observed within expected limits (no cache thrash).
Smoke tests: run the green-path prompt set (5 prompts per model family) and validate outputs against golden regexes or structural constraints; at least 90% pass rate.
Gating: if any model fails load or API health returns critical errors, autocheck marks deployment as FAILED and creates failure artifact with logs and suggested remediation steps.
Integration: outputs are consumed by the deploy orchestration (canary gate) so downstream steps can act on the summary (promote, rollback, or alert).
test_plan_steps: 1) Terraform apply completes and emits deploy metadata (stack_id, region, instance_ips, tls_cert_id).
2) Deployment orchestrator POSTs metadata to autocheck service endpoint with signed token (short-lived).

3) Autocheck executes: a) TLS handshake and cert validation to the API LB endpoint, b) calls /healthz and /metadata endpoints with service token, c) verifies auth (OIDC/SAML token exchange flow smoke), d) runs model-load probe via admin RPC to request model instance to load given model ref.
4) Run KV cache warmup: sequentially send warmup prefixes for each model family (configurable seedset) and capture per-request token latency and cache hit counters via metrics endpoint.
5) Run smoke inference suite: send 5 small prompts per model family with streaming disabled; validate response shape, length, presence of deterministic markers, and latency thresholds.
6) Aggregate metrics and logs: JFR-style mini-trace, kernel selection logs, and GPU memory usage snapshots from node exporters.
7) Publish summary JSON to artifact bucket and index in deployment run record; if failure, attach failing request traces and a short remediation checklist.
8) Emit appropriate webhook to CI/CD (promote or trigger rollback playbook) and send Slack channel notification to #vpc-deploys with short result summary and link to full artifact.
9) Mark the Linear ticket with a short progress update and tag related PRs for follow-up if flaky results observed.
10) Periodic: schedule a follow-up synthetic-run 30 minutes after initial pass to catch slow-converging models (configurable backoff and retries).
rollback_triggers: Any model fails to load within timeout (90s) in 50%+ of nodes for the model family.
API health endpoint returns non-200 or missing required metadata fields.
Smoke suite fail rate > 10% for any pinned model family.
KV cache thrash: eviction rate > configured threshold or sustained OOM warnings from the runtime.
Critical auth/TLS failures preventing normal client handshake.
Manual abort from on-call after triage within 10 minutes of failure alert.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Ava. Initial scope and acceptance criteria drafted.
2026-03-03: Design review with Infra and Runtime teams. Decided to reuse existing /admin/model/load RPC and extend it to return load-phase diagnostics (gpu_allocations, quant_mode).
2026-03-05: Liam prototyped autocheck service and a terraform null_resource hook to POST deployment metadata. Pushed prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-deploy/pull/429.
2026-03-09: First end-to-end run in staging: autocheck detected one model variant with delayed mmap page faults causing load timeouts; captured trace and attached logs for runtime team.
2026-03-10: Patch applied to runtime to increase mmap prefetch threshold; retested locally. Updating ticket to reflect in-progress verification in staging.
Next: expand golden regexes for smoke outputs and add OIDC exchange check into the auth smoke step.
notifications: autocheck success -> slack:#vpc-deploys 'Autocheck succeeded for stack_id=stack-77 in eu-west-1'
autocheck fail -> slack:#vpc-deploy-alerts 'Autocheck FAILED for stack_id=stack-77: model-load-timeout'
artifact upload -> ci/cd pipeline to decide promote/rollback
notes: Keep autocheck lightweight: target max runtime 3 minutes for small stacks, 10 minutes for larger clusters (configurable).
We intentionally avoid large-scale load tests here — this is a fast conformance gate. Full soak/load run is handled by separate job ENG-167891.
Consider adding a 'fast-fallback' path that tries compatible smaller quantized variants if primary model fails to load, to minimize customer impact for critical deploys.
Follow-up: add heuristics to trust successive autocheck runs less if noise spike observed (tunable confidence window).
